claim: High perceptual load cuts or eliminates distractor (flanker) interference in Lavie-lab studies: in Forster and Lavie (2008) the congruency effect was 36 ms at low load vs -4 ms at high load with displays shown until response (Exp 1, N=16), and the elimination also held with 100 ms displays (Exp 2a/2b, N=16 each).
agent_test: none
audit_note: In Forster and Lavie 2008 the 36 ms vs -4 ms (N=16) comes from Exp 1, where the display stayed on until response; the brief 100 ms displays (Exp 2a/2b, N=16 each) are a separate experiment with different values (about 25 vs -7 ms in Exp 2a per the researcher notes, not re-read from the table).
claim_before_audit: Under brief displays, high perceptual load cuts distractor (flanker) interference in the original lab studies (e.g. 36 ms low vs -4 ms high, N=16).

claim: The load effect on distractor interference does NOT replicate reliably: six online experiments (N 18-36 each) found no shrink at high load (56 vs 67 ms; interaction p=.98 in Exp 1), and earlier work found it absent or reversed under longer or masked displays. (Snowden et al. 2025 and Snowden and Gray 2025 are one paper.)
agent_test: none

claim: Whether the load effect appears depends on design: display duration/response-terminated, blocked vs interleaved load, previous-trial load, and what is held in visual memory. In the originating lab, intermixing load levels cut the detection effect from a d' drop of 1.8 (blocked) to 0.3 (Macdonald and Lavie 2008). Snowden's authors name interleaving and duration as candidate reasons for their null but could not confirm either.
agent_test: Vary context-block design (blocked vs mixed difficulty) in an LLM distractor test and check if the effect flips.

claim: Load was never defined independently of its effect (circular), and set-size load is confounded with dilution by neutral items; dilution itself works only under broad focus, same-category neutrals and unknown targets.
agent_test: Compare many neutral items with an easy task against a hard task with the same items in an LLM prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Few individuals show the load pattern and the same person flips between sessions (15% match in RT across five experiments; 7/20 in a new one); trial-level reliability is unclear even with hierarchical Bayesian models (2026 abstract: group effect robust, test-retest reliability not pinned down at practical trial counts; full text not opened).
agent_test: Run each prompt condition on many items and report per-item flip rates, not only means.

claim: High perceptual load increases inattentional blindness and deafness for unexpected stimuli (e.g. 21/28 vs 7/28 aware of a tone), and in a detection task it lowers sensitivity (d') rather than shifting criterion; results come from multiple experiments across Lavie-lab papers and a review (Lavie, Beck & Konstantinou 2014).
agent_test: Give an LLM a hard main task plus one planted off-topic salient item; compare noticing rate vs an easy main task at equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers and sensitivity finding verified (Macdonald & Lavie 2008 d' drop with no criterion change; 2011 21/28 vs 7/28), but none of the listed sources is a meta-analysis, so 'meta-analyses agree on the direction' is unsupported (also the notes swap beta: source has 9.0 high vs 5.5 low).
claim_before_audit: High perceptual load increases inattentional blindness and deafness for unexpected stimuli (e.g. 21/28 vs 7/28 aware of a tone), by lowering sensitivity not just criterion; meta-analyses agree on the direction.

claim: The inattentional-blindness effect of perceptual load shrinks or disappears when a cognitive-load task is added, so perceptual and cognitive load interact.
agent_test: Cross main-task difficulty with a side-task load in the scaffold.

claim: Working-memory/cognitive-control load has the opposite effect to perceptual load: it raises distractor processing (meta-analysis r=.20; 35 of 49 experiments up, 14 down).
agent_test: Fill the context with held-in-mind items (long task state) and check intrusion of irrelevant content.
audit_note: Entries a27, b09, b10 are the same de Fockert 2013 review (one source); numbers verified there (26 studies/49 experiments, r=.202, 35 up vs 14 down) and direction independently confirmed by Lavie, Beck & Konstantinou 2014.

claim: Load effects can occur without awareness: V1 response to invisible images fell under high load (N=7), and subliminal word priming was gated by task load (n=20 per experiment).
agent_test: Not directly testable on an LLM.

claim: The pooled load effect on the auditory mismatch negativity is small and fragile (k=6, N=97, -0.46 uV; power .15-.41).
agent_test: none

claim: A held memory cue captured early attention (P1) at both loads but behavioural capture vanished at high load; distractor salience cost appeared only at low target load, with higher alpha suppression at high load (MEG, N=30).
agent_test: Check whether planted salient distractors intrude less in hard than in easy tasks (the S1 prediction).

claim: High load also reduces task-unrelated thoughts (61.6% vs 48.9% probes; 57.5% vs 44.0%; Exp 4, N=20: 51.90% low vs 41.25% high, t(19)=3.43, d=1.57); small samples (N=10-20). The table row in Exp 4 that appeared to show the reverse order is a mislabelled table: the text says high load gave 41.25%.
agent_test: none

claim: Capacity for awareness under load grows with age (children miss more at a moderate load); ADHD shows different effects of cognitive vs perceptual load.
agent_test: none

claim: High load impairs peripheral memory and raises suggestibility in an applied museum event (peripheral objects 49.8% vs 9.4%; N=111).
agent_test: none

claim: Mechanism candidates for load: contrast-gain shift (threshold 18% vs 27%, N=14), biased competition, saliency-map model; rivals (salience, similarity, grouping) fit the same data.
agent_test: none

claim: One irrelevant sentence in grade-school math sharply lowers LLM accuracy; at most 18% of originally solved problems stay solved under all distractor types (code-davinci-002 CoT micro 72.4, macro 6.0).
agent_test: Insert one irrelevant sentence into our benchmark items; measure macro accuracy across variants at equal tokens.
audit_note: Shi et al. abstract says 'no more than 18%' and Table 3 gives code-davinci-002 COT micro 72.4 / macro 6.0; the three Shi entries are one paper, so the specific figures rest on a single source (Yoran 2023 only loosely supports the general point).

claim: What hurts an LLM is similarity to the task, not mere presence: in-topic and role-overlap distractors hurt most (micro 63.1 vs 80.7); related high-scoring non-answer documents cut accuracy up to 25 percent while random unrelated documents often help.
agent_test: Compare near-topic vs off-topic distractors at equal token count in S1 context building.
audit_note: Verified in Shi et al. (COT micro in-topic 63.1 vs off-topic 80.7; role overlap 68.3 vs 76.6) and Cuconasu et al. (peak -0.24, -25% with one distracting document; random documents up to +35%); independent authors.

claim: Random unrelated documents added to a RAG prompt raised Llama2 accuracy by up to 0.07 (+35%) with 4 retrieved documents (2023-24 result). On later models it does not generalise: neutral appended filler of equal length did not hurt Gemini 2.0 Flash (0.82 vs 0.85, p=.45) but interleaved irrelevant text did (0.72 at 80%); a 299K-character irrelevant context cut a gpt-5.4-mini agent from 8/10 to 3/10 passes; whitespace padding alone cost 13.9% to 85%.
agent_test: Replicate with a current model at equal tokens, separating appended neutral filler from interleaved irrelevant text.

claim: In LLMs the distraction effect does not shrink with task load; it stays or grows. Yang 2025: error power-law exponent 0.11 at 2 steps to 0.49 at 5 steps, step accuracy 43% to 19% from 1 to 15 distractors. CogniLoad (22 models incl. gpt-5, o3, gemini-2.5-pro): the distractor dip deepens as intrinsic difficulty rises. CatAttack shows larger relative harm on easy problems (5.33x vs 1.80x for R1) but that comes from near-zero baselines. All grids use synthetic or text tasks, not Lavie's perceptual load.
agent_test: Check whether distractor cost grows with problem depth in our own tasks, in absolute accuracy points; if so do not assume hard tasks are protected.
audit_note: Yang 2025 (0.11 to 0.49 for Grok-3-Beta, 43% to 19% at 5 steps), CogniLoad (U-shape more pronounced as d increases), CatAttack (5.33x easy vs 1.80x hard for R1, authors attribute to low baseline) all verified; minor: claim omits that the 43%->19% figure is Grok-3-Beta at depth 5.

claim: Long context hurts even with perfect retrieval or irrelevant padding: accuracy depends on position (U-shape, 56.1% closed-book vs 88.3% oracle, drop over 20 points mid-context), length (GPT-4o 99.3 to 69.7 at 32K), padding (0.92 to 0.68), and gold passage size (Gemini 48% small vs 73% large). Confirmed on 2025-26 models: masked or whitespace padding costs 13.9% to 85%; Opus 4.6 recall of an obvious planted action 99.7% at 100K vs 69% at 800K, worst in the middle; frontier monitors miss subtle actions 2x to 30x more after 800K benign tokens.
agent_test: Keep the working context short and place the key item at the start or end; compare long vs short context at equal tokens.
audit_note: All figures verified (Liu 56.1/88.3 and >20 point drop; FLenQA 0.92 to 0.68; NoLiMa GPT-4o 99.3 to 69.7 at 32K; Bianchi Gemini 48% to 73%; Du 13.9%-85% incl. whitespace/masked; Martin & Roger 99.7% vs 69%, 2x-30x); Du's 'perfect retrieval' effect is per paper, not all items.

claim: A scaffold that regenerates only the relevant context before answering beats plain prompting: S2A 62.8 to 80.3 (TriviaQA, opinionated) and 51.7 to 61.3 on in-topic distractors; keeping the original text drops it to 74.5; Thread of Thought also beats vanilla on chaotic contexts; ATF analyse-then-filter COT 50.2 to 74.9 on GPT-3.5. At equal total tokens the case is unproven: Focused CoT matches plain CoT accuracy with half the tokens including extraction but on clean problems; context management in 2026 search agents buys accuracy with more tool calls; an oracle distractor-aware filter is free on Claude 4.x and GPT-5.5 (upper bound).
agent_test: Add a rewrite-context-to-relevant-facts step and compare to plain on a planted-distractor set at equal total tokens (extra pass counted per G7).
audit_note: S2A (62.8->80.3, 51.7->61.3, keep-original 74.5), ThoT (best on PopQA), ATF (COT 50.2->74.9 on GPT-3.5-Turbo), Focused CoT (2-3x fewer tokens, extraction counted), Xia 2026 (context management as test-time scaling) and Arjmandi 2026 all verified; minor: the oracle filter gains are significant only for Haiku/Sonnet, Opus and GPT-5.5 sit at ceiling (+0.008, +0.017), and 'free' is the notes' reading, not a measured cost.

claim: An ignore-irrelevant-information instruction gives inconsistent gains and depends on distractor type. Helps on generic off-topic trivia: appended ignore line cut CatAttack success 37.5% to 9.9% on Llama-3.1-8B. Helps when suspect conditions are named and verified (I3C, +11.7 on GSM-IC2-1K, GPT-3.5). Does not help on in-topic or adversarial context: bare ignore instruction lowered accuracy when irrelevant text was on-topic (GPT-3.5), and guidance changed 7 models by -0.013 to +0.026 under adaptive distraction (GPT-4o +0.002, Claude-3.5-sonnet -0.013). Earlier: +5.4 micro in GSM-IC code-davinci-002 CoT, none consistent for LLaMA-2-70B. No test yet on 2026 models.
agent_test: A/B an ignore-instruction at equal tokens on several current models, with off-topic and in-topic distractors separately.

claim: Self-consistency sampling recovers much distractor loss (COT micro 88.1, LTM 93.4) and the correct answer is in 20 samples for 99.7% of problems, yet best macro accuracy is only 45%.
agent_test: Use code to pick among samples; test whether distractor variants break agreement.

claim: Narrow task instructions can make models omit a co-present critical item (report rates 0.08-0.53 vs about 1.00 open; strict exclusive instruction 0.00), a machine analogue of inattentional blindness; single-author preprint. On three flagship models (24 scenarios each): GPT-5 0.00 and Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.00-0.09 vs 1.00 open, Opus 4.8 0.83-0.96 (robust). Reasoning did not remove it.
agent_test: Compare focused vs open instructions for a planted critical item in our scaffold.

claim: The omission effect is a threshold on output scope, not a graded load gradient: one narrow sub-question switches it on (report 1.00 to near 0); model family predicted it better than scale. Output length was 189 characters with one question vs 1,770 open. The study did not test an appended one-line open sentence, so whether a free fix exists is unknown; the tested fix (a second open-ended critic pass) restored 1.00 at the cost of one inference.
agent_test: Test 'also list anything unrequested but critical' appended to a narrow task, and an output-schema field for it, on 65 or more items per cell.

claim: Injected instructions act like capturing distractors in attention heads, and attention noise from irrelevant context can be cancelled architecturally (Differential Transformer, 30-point gap on multi-needle at 4K), but these need model internals.
agent_test: Not testable on a prompt-only agent.

claim: Working memory in ChatGPT has capacity about 3 on n-back, and ignorable noise symbols lower it significantly; chain-of-thought helps spatial tasks.
agent_test: none

claim: Overloading an LLM with extra task demands can bypass safety behaviour (cognitive overload jailbreak); numbers not verified.
agent_test: none

claim: No study manipulates perceptual load on an LLM the way Lavie does, but several now vary load types in controlled grids: CogniLoad (difficulty x length x distractor ratio, 22 models), ICE (20/50/80% irrelevant tokens with length-matched control), a dual-task paradigm (GPT-4o, o3-mini, o4-mini shift to plausibility). arXiv 2603.00270 (interference) and 2601.11585 (context selection) were opened and are not load studies. None shows a Lavie-style shield.
agent_test: Design: easy vs hard main task, same planted off-topic distractor, equal tokens, 65 or more items per cell, code-scored.

claim: Frontier models used as monitors miss a planted dangerous action more often when it sits in a long benign transcript, worst in the middle (Opus 4.6 99.7% to 69% at 100K vs 800K; padding both sides took a non-thinking Opus to 5%); thinking and short reminders (under 3% extra tokens) help for obvious needles but not subtle attacks.
agent_test: Plant a critical item in long context at several positions; compare periodic reminders vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Cheap structured prompts beat free-form self-checks for catching omissions: a detailed external checklist passed 10/10 vs 5/10 for a generic self-check (p=0.0325, gpt-5.4-mini); asking the monitor to list suspicious items first raised detection for few extra tokens; an external open-ended critic pass restored every omitted finding.
agent_test: Replace generic 'check everything' with a code-held checklist; test against a list-first step.

claim: In the studies reviewed, none found that a harder main task makes a planted off-topic distractor intrude less at equal length. Harm stays or grows with intrinsic difficulty in synthetic text tasks (CogniLoad, Yang 2025), is not strongly tied to the complexity of the injected task (distractor injection attacks, which vary distractor not main-task difficulty), and in MedDistractQA is smaller for stronger models (baseline accuracy predicts robustness; task hardness was not varied). The only counter-pattern is a floor effect in relative error (CatAttack). Lavie's shield is therefore not a safe default for S1, though none of these studies test perceptual load.
agent_test: Report absolute accuracy loss by difficulty tier in our own tasks.
audit_note: CogniLoad (U-shape deepens with difficulty), Yang 2025 and CatAttack floor effect check out, but Zhang et al. vary the injected distractor's complexity (not the main task's difficulty), MedDistractQA never varies task hardness (it only shows baseline accuracy predicts robustness), and 'no 2025-26 study finds' is an unprovable universal negative.
claim_before_audit: Gap 1 answer: no 2025-26 study finds that a harder main task makes a planted off-topic distractor intrude less at equal length. Harm stays or grows with difficulty (CogniLoad, Yang 2025), is as large for complex as simple injected tasks (distractor injection), and shrinks with model strength not task hardness (MedDistractQA). The only counter-pattern is a floor effect in relative error. Lavie's shield is not a safe default for S1.

claim: Distractor-aware truncation (keeping signal, dropping all else) preserves or raises accuracy on Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 (Haiku +0.083, Sonnet +0.104 on BABILong, p_adj<=.003), while naive middle truncation collapses scores because it removes the signal. This is an oracle upper bound for any context filter.
agent_test: Measure how close a model-run filter gets to oracle filtering.

claim: The Snowden 2025 null is partly a design question (interleaved load, short displays, one stimulus set, online) and partly unexplained: the originating lab's own data show intermixing cuts the effect about six times (d' drop 1.8 blocked vs 0.3), the authors cannot say why their displays differ, and their individual-level supplement mirrors the group null. Reliability of the effect is also unclear at practical trial counts.
agent_test: Weight the human load literature as conditional on blocked designs.

claim: The 2007 Cartwright-Finch and Lavie awareness numbers remain unverified (paywalled). A later adaptation by the same group found adult awareness 15/16 at low load vs 2/16 at high load (chi-square 21.20, p<.01), and the 2008 Macdonald and Lavie review says awareness is typically 40-50% lower at high load, consistent with the 55% vs 10% second-hand figures.
agent_test: none

claim: Explicit dual-task load (arithmetic interleaved with a sentence) shifts GPT-4o, o3-mini and o4-mini toward plausibility-based answers, a human-like heuristic shift under load; a side task can push a model to shortcuts.
agent_test: Check whether adding a side task in the scaffold raises plausible-but-wrong answers.

claim: Capability, not task hardness, predicts distraction resistance: proprietary models lost 3.7-3.8% vs 10.6-10.9% for open models on MedDistractQA (baseline accuracy r2=.49-.58), though Qwen3-4B beat Qwen3-8B and prompt guidance did not help; reasoning models are the best defended but still lose accuracy.
agent_test: none
